newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks trade down in morning.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks trade down in morning.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks opened weak on Wednesday in a follow-through of Tuesday's sell-off and due to the absence of positive news, brokers said.
But the market was expected to pick up later in the day prompted by Wall Street's better performance, they said.

"I expect a pick up on the back of Wall Street," said a broker with a large regional house. "I think the selling has been a little bit overdone. There was no real reason to be down the way we were yesterday."
The Hang Seng Index was 19 points lower at 13,434 after 45 minutes of trade on healthy turnover of HK$1.60 billion.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 51.57 points to 6,858.11, with all the gains coming late in the session and prompted by program trading.
In Hong Kong, brokers said derivatives-related trading was exaggerating market movements.

"With futures continuing to trade at a discount, there is some unwinding of derivative trading (positions)," said Antony Mak, sales director at Vickers Ballas, adding that the rising volume of derivative activity had increased volatility.

Hang Seng Index futures, while still trading at a discount to the cash market, firmed after the open. The February contract was trading 15 points lower at 13,365 and the March contract five points down at 13,380.
The property sector showed a modest gain, outperforming the broad market in early trade, while all other blue chip sectors trended in negative territory.
H shares and red chips also were mostly higher.
Sun Hung Kai Property, after falling sharply in the previous two trading sessions, added HK$0.75 to trade at HK$89.00. Cheung Kong rose HK$0.25 to HK$74.00.
International banking giant HSBC Holdings shed HK$0.50 to HK$186.50 and subsidiary Hang Seng Bank lost HK$0.25 to HK$91.25. Ka Wah Bank dipped HK$0.075 to HK$3.70.
CITIC Pacific eased HK$0.10 to HK$38.40, while China Resources inched up HK$0.15 to HK$16.20. China Pharmaceutical put on HK$0.02 to HK$1.16.
Among the H shares, Shandong Xinhua jumped HK$0.075 to HK$2.125. Guangdong Kelon leaped HK$0.20 to HK$6.20. China Eastern rose HK$0.04 to HK$1.42.
